content: Ammonium thiocyanate and sodium thiocyanate are chemical compounds, with sodium thiocyanate having the formula NaSCN. This compound is a colorless, deliquescent salt and serves as one of the primary sources of the thiocyanate anion. Due to this property, it is widely utilized as a precursor in the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and other specialty chemicals. Thiocyanate salts, such as sodium thiocyanate, are typically synthesized through the reaction of cyanide with elemental sulfur. Sodium thiocyanate crystallizes in an orthorhombic lattice structure. In this structure, each sodium ion (Na⁺) is coordinated by three sulfur atoms and three nitrogen atoms, which are provided by the triatomic thiocyanate anion. Applications in Chemical Synthesis Sodium thiocyanate (NaSCN) is commonly used to convert alkyl halides into their corresponding alkyl thiocyanates. Related reagents, such as ammonium thiocyanate and potassium thiocyanate, are also employed in similar reactions. Notably, potassium thiocyanate exhibits twice the solubility in water compared to sodium thiocyanate. Silver thiocyanate can also be used in these reactions, as the precipitation of insoluble silver halides simplifies the reaction workup process. For example, when isopropyl bromide is treated with sodium thiocyanate in a hot ethanolic solution, isopropyl thiocyanate is produced. Sodium thiocyanate can also be used to generate reactive species in situ, which can then react with organic amines to form thiourea derivatives.
